artifacts.summary: Evaluates the three routes and selects route (a): targeted 2-page re-OCR drops joyce_1999 from 4 hits to 2 (below the >=3 threshold) with zero gate/exemption/threshold changes; rejects routes (b) and (c) with reasoning, and recommends an additive docstring/guide reconciliation plus a 104-executes/105-owns-tooling split.

memory_candidates.content: When a quality-gate rejection is driven by a small count of hits over a threshold, check whether the rejection is composed of distinct sub-classes (genuine defects vs. benign-but-unexempted noise) before reaching for a regex-exemption fix. If fixing only the genuine-defect sub-class already drops the count below threshold, no gate/exemption change is needed at all -- the benign sub-class never needs to be matched or tolerated by the check. This avoids the risk of overfitting an exemption regex to a handful of non-generalizable false-positive strings (e.g. garbled OCR renderings of math notation with no shared structural shape).

In the literature extension, 'scanned vs. born-digital' is not a safe document-class boundary for calibration or tier-selection decisions -- task 102 established the real discriminator is defect origin (primary-tier structuring artifact vs. text-layer/OCR-vintage defect), which requires inspecting where post-conversion hits fall rather than being computable from document metadata. Any future task proposing a scanned/OCR-keyed threshold or calibration class should check this precedent first, since known scanned/OCR documents in the corpus (hott_book_2013, ahrens_north) are correctly-rejected genuine-corruption cases that a class-wide threshold bump would risk un-rejecting.
